1.title: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy
1.context: The same three senders as the first letter, writing close behind it. Silvanus is Silas’s fuller Roman name; the greeting is unchanged because the relationship is.
1.question: When you write to the same people twice, what do you most want them to hear the second time?

1.title: Obligated to Thank God
1.context: Obligated frames the thanksgiving as a debt owed to evidence. Growing more and more is a living word: the faith is mid-growth, not finished or failing.
1.question: Whose growth do you owe God thanks for, out loud?

1.title: We Boast Among God’s Churches
1.context: The founding team carried this church’s story to other congregations as an example. The boast is perseverance and faith under persecution, not size or success.
1.question: What would other people say your perseverance looks like?

1.title: Clear Evidence
1.context: Evidence is a courtroom word. The endurance itself is the exhibit that God’s judgment is righteous, and the sufferers are counted worthy of the kingdom they suffer for.
1.question: What is your suffering evidence of, in your own reading of it?

1.title: Only Right
1.context: Repayment in this letter is about God’s righteousness, not the church’s revenge. The settling of accounts is deliberately left in God’s hand, and the next episode shows both its edges.
1.question: What account do you need to leave in God’s hand instead of your own?

2.title: Relief, and to Us as Well
2.context: Relief is dated to the revelation of the Lord Jesus, not to improved circumstances. The writers include themselves among the oppressed who will be relieved.
2.question: What relief are you waiting for that only the Lord’s coming will finally bring?

2.title: Blazing Fire
2.context: Those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel are the two descriptions of the judged. Eternal destruction is defined as separation from the presence of the Lord.
2.question: How does this passage change the way you pray for people who afflict others?

2.title: Glorified in His Saints
2.context: Including you ties the afflicted congregation into the day’s glory by name, on one ground: they believed the testimony the team brought.
2.question: What does it mean to you that Christ is glorified in his people, not only shown to them?

2.title: We Always Pray for You
2.context: Always pray is the interval’s work between now and the revelation. The glorifying runs in both directions: the name glorified in them, and they in Him.
2.question: Who is praying this kind of prayer for you, and who are you praying it for?

3.title: A Letter Seeming to Be From Us
3.context: Spirit, message, and letter cover every channel of the day: a prophetic utterance, a spoken report, and a written forgery trading on the team’s name.
3.question: What alarming claim about God have you had to test rather than simply absorb?

3.title: It Will Not Come Until
3.context: The order given is checkable and public: the rebellion first, then the revealing. A day with prerequisites cannot have arrived in secret.
3.question: Where do you need the calm of checking the order of things before you panic?

3.title: Proclaiming Himself to Be God
3.context: The letter gives the figure’s program, not his name or date: opposition to every so-called god, and a seat in God’s temple, proclaiming himself to be God.
3.question: What does self-exaltation look like in ordinary life, far from any temple?

3.title: Do You Not Remember?
3.context: The sequence was founding teaching, delivered in person. The appeal is to the church’s own memory, not to new information.
3.question: What were you taught early in faith that you most need to remember right now?

4.title: You Know What Is Restraining
4.context: The letter assumes its first readers know the restraint from Paul’s in-person teaching and never repeats it in writing. Every identification offered since is a guess; the text names none.
4.question: How do you live faithfully with a question the text deliberately leaves open?

4.title: Already at Work, Until
4.context: The mystery of lawlessness is a hidden working, already active, while the revealing waits on the restrainer’s removal. Both are true in the same verse.
4.question: What does it change to believe evil is both active and restrained right now?

4.title: The Breath of His Mouth
4.context: No battle is described. Breath and the majesty of the arrival end the lawless one: the disproportion is the point.
4.question: What overwhelming thing in your life might look different next to the majesty of his arrival?

4.title: They Refused the Love of the Truth
4.context: Power, sign, and false wonder borrow the vocabulary of true miracles and are marked false by their source and aim. Refused is the hinge: the truth was offered in love.
4.question: What truth have you been tempted to refuse because loving it would cost you?

4.title: A Powerful Delusion
4.context: The delusion is presented as judgment on a prior refusal: believing the lie follows disbelieving the truth and delighting in wickedness.
4.question: Where do you need to love the truth early, before refusal hardens?

5.title: Chosen From the Beginning
5.context: Two instruments are named together: the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth. The same truth refused in verse 10 is believed here, and the letter sets the groups side by side.
5.question: Which do you think about more, God’s choosing or your believing? Why?

5.title: Called Through Our Gospel
5.context: Our gospel ties the eternal choice to a few weeks of preaching in Thessalonica. The goal is sharing in the glory of the Lord Jesus Christ.
5.question: Who first brought the gospel to you, and what do you owe their faithfulness?

5.title: Stand Firm and Cling
5.context: By speech or by letter quietly answers the forgery alarm: the genuine traditions are known by their content, whichever channel carried them.
5.question: What teaching do you most need to cling to in a noisy season?

5.title: Eternal Comfort and Good Hope
5.context: The prayer closes the storm chapter with comfort aimed at ordinary life: hearts encouraged and strengthened in every good word and deed.
5.question: What good word or deed do you need your heart strengthened for this week?

6.title: Pray for Us
6.context: Spread quickly is a runner’s word for the word’s advance. The Lord is faithful stands between the prayer requests and the commands, holding both.
6.question: Who is carrying the word somewhere hard, and how will you pray for them today?

6.title: We Were Not Undisciplined Among You
6.context: Undisciplined is a soldier’s word for a man out of ranks. The team’s waived right and night-and-day work are cited as precedent, not as pride.
6.question: What right have you waived to set an example, and was it worth it?

6.title: He Shall Not Eat
6.context: Unwilling is the rule’s key word: refusal, not inability. The busybodies are busy in everyone’s affairs but their own work.
6.question: Where are you busy in other people’s matters while your own work waits?

6.title: Admonish Him as a Brother
6.context: Withdrawal and brotherhood are commanded together: distance aimed at a shame that restores, never at enmity.
6.question: Who do you need to admonish as a brother, and who have you been treating as an enemy instead?

6.title: My Mark in Every Letter
6.context: After a warning about a forged letter, Paul displays his authenticating mark on purpose. Peace at all times is prayed over a church told to expect affliction.
6.question: What is the mark the people who know you would recognize as genuinely yours?
